about: Pixel sizes and listing rules per delivery surface. Dated data, no code. A number that was not read from the official page on verified_on is null and listed under unverified.

jpeg.notes: The byte budget of a JPEG export on a target whose max_bytes is null. It is a working limit of this skill, not a platform rule: the lowest cap any web surface here states (LinkedIn, X), so a file under it also passes a console that later names one. A target with a max_bytes uses that instead.

play-feature.safe_insets: Google draws the cutoff zones in a 406x198 diagram and states no number for them. The insets are that diagram measured on 2026-09-22 (left 61 px, right 59 px, top 29 px, bottom 31 px of 406x198), so about 15 percent per edge; the wording they follow is quoted in the row's notes
appstore-header.max_bytes: the creative assets specification states no byte cap
appstore-search.max_bytes: the creative assets specification states no byte cap
appstore-universal.max_bytes: the creative assets specification states no byte cap
appstore-header.max_count, appstore-search.max_count, appstore-universal.max_count: Apple states no count; a placement shows one asset per product page and language

appstore-header.safe_insets, appstore-search.safe_insets, appstore-universal.safe_insets: Apple's pages ask for key elements inside a safe area but publish no number; the area exists only in Apple's downloadable templates. The insets are the 'Art Safe Area' rectangles of the Sketch template (creative_assets-templates.sketch, linked from the asset best-practices page, file dated 2026-08-28) read on 2026-10-07: header 1646x661 at x 1097, y 493 of 3840x1646; search results 2168x1030 at x 836, y 765 of 3840x2560; universal 1402x962 at x 1921, y 660 of 5244x2950, centred across but above the middle. The template is not redistributed here
appstore-search.allowed.ratio: Apple names 3:2 and a size range; whether a file a pixel off 3:2 passes is not stated, so validate wants the exact ratio
email-card: no sending platform or mail client states a size for an image card; 1208x680 (a 604x340 slot in a 680 px email with 38 px gutters, at 2x) is this project's choice
email-card.sheet_width: no client states how wide a phone shows the content column; 320 px is about a phone's column inside its gutters

appstore-header.sheet_width, appstore-search.sheet_width: Apple states no display size for either placement. Measured on 2026-10-12 from Apple's demo videos on the asset best-practices page: on an iPhone in portrait the header shows at about 1.55:1, roughly the centre two thirds of its width, with the back and share buttons over its top corners; the search results asset shows whole, as a rounded 3:2 card about 343 pt wide. The search sheet is that card; the header sheet shows the whole canvas at 400 px, about an iPhone's width, so it reads smaller there than on the phone, where the visible two thirds fill that width

appstore-iphone-69.label: App Store iPhone 6.9 inch
appstore-iphone-69.required_when: iPhone apps: this set or the 6.5-inch set
appstore-iphone-69.notes: 1 to 10 screenshots per device size. JPEG or PNG, no alpha. App Review 2.3.3: screenshots show the app in use.

appstore-iphone-65.label: App Store iPhone 6.5 inch
appstore-iphone-65.required_when: iPhone apps when no 6.9-inch set is provided
appstore-iphone-65.notes: Required only when no 6.9 inch set is provided. JPEG or PNG, no alpha.

appstore-iphone-63.label: App Store iPhone 6.3 inch
appstore-iphone-63.notes: Optional when the 6.9 inch set exists. JPEG or PNG, no alpha.

appstore-ipad-13.label: App Store iPad 13 inch
appstore-ipad-13.notes: 1 to 10 screenshots. JPEG or PNG, no alpha.

appstore-mac.label: Mac App Store screenshot
appstore-mac.notes: One of 1280x800, 1440x900, 2560x1600 or 2880x1800, 16:10. 1 to 10 screenshots, JPEG or PNG, no alpha. The page lists no portrait size for Mac, so the target is landscape only. 2880x1800 is this project's render size: the largest listed.

appstore-header.label: App Store product page header (creative asset)

video.audio: muted by default; the viewer may unmute it on the product page

appstore-header.notes: Top of the product page, on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 or later; optional, separate from screenshots. 21:9 at 3840x1646 as JPEG or PNG, or 16:9 at 5244x2950 as PNG only (that file is the universal asset, appstore-universal). No alpha. Apple's guidance: one clear idea for a first-time visitor, no clutter; text optional, short and localised per language; focal point in the centre and key elements inside the art safe area, because devices and orientations crop the header differently (safe_insets, from Apple's template). An iPhone in portrait shows about the centre two thirds of the width (unverified, from Apple's demo videos), so the sheet judges the whole canvas at 400 px. Content: no prices, discounts, URLs or copyright symbols, no unverified awards, no Apple recognitions (Editors' Choice, App of the Day, Game of the Day, Apple Design Award), no logos or mentions of other platforms or marketplaces, 4+ whatever the app's age rating. The video variant (`video`) is not rendered here.

appstore-search.label: App Store search results asset (creative asset)

video.audio: muted in search results, and the viewer cannot unmute it

appstore-search.notes: The app's tile in App Store search results, on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 or later; optional. Set, it takes the place of the screenshots and previews there; without it in-app events, previews and screenshots show as before. 3:2 from 1920x1280 to 3840x2560 as JPEG or PNG (3840x2560 is this project's render size), or 16:9 at 5244x2950 as PNG only (the universal asset). No alpha. Apple's guidance: make the app's purpose obvious at a glance and show the real experience (interface, content, gameplay); text optional, short and localised; key elements inside the art safe area (safe_insets, from Apple's template). An iPhone shows it whole as a 3:2 card about 343 pt wide (unverified, from Apple's demo videos), the sheet's true size. Same content rules as the header. The video variant (`video`) is not rendered here.

appstore-universal.label: App Store universal creative asset (header and search results)
appstore-universal.notes: One 16:9 image at 5244x2950, PNG only, that both placements accept: App Store Connect offers 'Use header asset in search results' only for a universal asset. No alpha. Apple recommends it for one recognisable brand across header and search results. Its art safe area in Apple's template is the smallest of the three: about 27 percent of the width, set above the middle (safe_insets). Apple's spec lists no universal video. Same content rules and OS floor as the header.

play-phone.label: Google Play phone screenshot
play-phone.recommended: 4 or more at 1080 px or larger (9:16 or 16:9) to be eligible for promotion
play-phone.notes: 1080x1920 is this project's render size inside the allowed range. Taglines at most 20% of the image. Google lists device imagery under content to avoid: frame none is the conservative choice.

play-tablet.label: Google Play tablet screenshot
play-tablet.required_when: the listing targets tablets or Chromebooks
play-tablet.notes: 1440x2560 is this project's render size inside the allowed range. Taglines at most 20% of the image. Play keeps a 7-inch and a 10-inch tablet slot under the same large-screen rules: this one set goes into both. Use play-tablet-7 and play-tablet-10 when the two slots get different screenshots.

play-tablet-7.label: Google Play 7-inch tablet screenshot
play-tablet-7.required_when: the listing fills the 7-inch tablet slot with its own screenshots
play-tablet-7.notes: Play lists tablets (7-inch and 10-inch) as device types with up to 8 screenshots each, and the Publisher API keeps them apart (sevenInchScreenshots, tenInchScreenshots). The help page states one rule set for large screens: at least 4, each side 1080 to 7680 px, 16:9 landscape or 9:16 portrait, no text outside the app experience. No size of its own for 7-inch: 1440x2560 is this project's render size.

play-tablet-10.label: Google Play 10-inch tablet screenshot
play-tablet-10.required_when: the listing fills the 10-inch tablet slot with its own screenshots
play-tablet-10.notes: Same large-screen rules as play-tablet-7 (at least 4, up to 8, each side 1080 to 7680 px, 16:9 or 9:16). No size of its own for 10-inch: 1440x2560 is this project's render size; a landscape set renders 2560x1440.

play-feature.label: Google Play feature graphic
play-feature.notes: JPEG or 24-bit PNG, no alpha. Taglines at most 20% of the image. Google asks for the brand logo, the app name, the primary slogan and the main UI outside the cutoff zones, for background elements only at the edges, and states that a graphic that ignores the focal point and the zones may become ineligible for the formats that add their own UI overlays. The zones are drawn, not numbered: `safe_insets` are the drawing measured (see unverified), so the safe box at 1024x500 is about x 154 to 876, y 73 to 422.

og.label: Open Graph link card (Facebook, LinkedIn, chat apps)
og.notes: Facebook: 200x200 at least, 1200x630 or more recommended, 1.91:1, at most 8 MB. LinkedIn: at least 1200x627, 1.91:1, at most 5 MB. The byte cap here is the lower of the two. Re-read on 2026-09-23: neither page states a maximum pixel size for link previews, and LinkedIn's page caps single-image ads at 7680x4320 (landscape), so the optional 2x render (2400x1260, `scales`) is bounded by the byte cap alone.

x-card.label: X summary card with large image
x-card.notes: 2:1, at least 300x157, at most 4096x4096, under 5 MB. The optional 2x render (2400x1200, `scales`) stays inside 4096x4096. No live official page exists on verified_on: every Cards URL redirects. The source is the last archived official copy (2026-01-12).

github-social.label: GitHub repository social preview
github-social.notes: PNG, JPG or GIF under 1 MB; at least 640x320, 1280x640 for best display (2:1). One image per repository, shared only from a public repository. GitHub accepts PNG transparency but recommends a solid background when unsure: this project renders opaque. Under 1 MB is read as 1 000 000 bytes, so a card with a photographic plate usually needs `export` jpg.

email-card.label: Email image card (a 604x340 slot at 2x)
email-card.notes: A card in the body of a marketing or product email, shown at 604x340: the content column of a 680 px email with 38 px gutters, about 16:9. No sending platform or mail client defines a card size, so the slot is this project's choice, rendered at twice its size for high-density screens. Customer.io: JPG, PNG or GIF through its editors, at most 4096 px a side and 2 MB, hosted images best under 1 MB. Mailchimp: templates 600 px wide (legacy builder) or 660 px (new builder), images best 600 to 1200 or 660 to 1320 px wide, at most 1 MB recommended. max_bytes is that shared 1 MB recommendation read as 1 000 000 bytes; a sending platform or review with a lower limit wins. The card shows at half its pixels on a desktop column and at about a quarter on a phone, so the sheet judges it at 320 px.

ph-gallery.label: Product Hunt gallery image
ph-gallery.notes: 1270x760 recommended, at least 2 images, no maximum stated on either page. The launch guide states 'All images, GIF or not, need to be under 3MB' in its thumbnail entry; its gallery entry and the help page name no byte limit for gallery images. max_bytes reads that sentence as covering every image of the post, and 3 MB as 3 000 000 bytes: the lower reading of both.

ph-thumbnail.label: Product Hunt thumbnail
ph-thumbnail.notes: Judged at 240, 80 and 40 px. The launch guide's thumbnail entry: 'All images, GIF or not, need to be under 3MB'; the help page states the 3 MB for a GIF thumbnail only. 3 MB read as 3 000 000 bytes, the lower reading.

cws-screenshot.label: Chrome Web Store screenshot
cws-screenshot.notes: 1280x800 (preferred) or 640x400, square corners, no padding (full bleed), at least 1 and up to 5. The store downscales every screenshot to 640x400, so copy must read at that size. Screenshots show the actual user experience and may be localised per locale.

cws-promo-small.label: Chrome Web Store small promo tile
cws-promo-small.notes: PNG or JPEG, 440x280, required; items without it are shown after items that have it. Promo tiles are not localised: one file for every locale, so text-free is the default. Google's advice: communicate the brand rather than repeat a screenshot, avoid text, work at half size, assume a light grey page, prefer saturated colours over white and light grey, fill the whole region, keep edges well defined.

cws-promo-marquee.label: Chrome Web Store marquee promo tile
cws-promo-marquee.notes: PNG or JPEG, 1400x560, optional, one per item; an item cannot be featured in the marquee without it. Not localised, reviewed before it shows (about a week). Same design advice as the small tile.

ad-feed-4x5.label: Ad, feed portrait 4:5 (Meta Feed, Google App campaigns portrait)
ad-feed-4x5.notes: Meta Ads Guide, app promotion: Feed image 4:5 at 1440x1800, JPG or PNG, at most 30 MB. Google App campaigns accept 4:5 (1200x1500 recommended, 320x400 minimum) as JPG or PNG up to 5 MB: the byte cap here is Google's. Google's best practices keep overlaid text and logos under 20 percent of the image. Meta asks non-9:16 Instagram feed ads to keep the bottom and the sides free of text; it publishes no numbers for that.

ad-square.label: Ad, square 1:1 (Meta Feed, Google App campaigns, TikTok carousel)
ad-square.notes: Google App campaigns: 1:1 at 1200x1200 (200x200 minimum), JPG or PNG up to 5 MB. Meta Help: 1:1 at 1080x1080 or larger. TikTok carousel images: 640x640 or larger. One 1200x1200 file satisfies all three.

ad-vertical-9x16.label: Ad, vertical 9:16 still (Meta Stories and Reels, TikTok carousel)
ad-vertical-9x16.notes: Meta Ads Guide: Stories and Reels image 9:16 at 1440x2560, JPG or PNG, at most 30 MB; keep roughly 14 percent at the top, 35 percent at the bottom and 6 percent on each side free of text and logos (Facebook Stories video: 14 and 20 percent). TikTok carousel images: 720x1280 or larger. TikTok publishes its in-feed safe zone only as downloadable templates: no numbers were read.

ad-landscape.label: Ad, landscape 1.91:1 (Google App campaigns, TikTok carousel and Ad Network)
ad-landscape.notes: Google App campaigns: 1.91:1 at 1200x628 (600x314 minimum), JPG or PNG up to 5 MB, overlaid text and logos under 20 percent. TikTok carousel and Ad Network images: 1200x628.

ad-video-9x16.label: Video ad canvas 9:16 (layers and end cards for TikTok, Reels, Stories, Shorts)
ad-video-9x16.notes: A still canvas for video assembly, not an upload: `layers` cuts the screen out so a real recording plays under the drawn frame. 9:16 is the vertical video ratio on Meta, TikTok (540x960 or larger) and Google App campaigns; Meta's Instagram Feed video page names 1080x1920. Safe insets are Meta's Stories and Reels numbers.

ad-video-16x9.label: Video ad canvas 16:9 (layers and end cards for YouTube and Google App campaigns)
ad-video-16x9.notes: A still canvas for video assembly, not an upload. Google App campaigns take 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1 videos through YouTube and publish no pixel size; TikTok asks 960x540 or larger for 16:9. 1920x1080 is this project's render size.
